key_insight: Resource-dependent dispatch constraints can preserve military microgrid readiness for prolonged outages while allowing economical grid-connected operation.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating battery energy, generator fuel, and load shifting helps operators sustain mission-critical loads despite uncertain demand, solar generation, and generator availability.
method: Compute a robust viability kernel defining resource combinations sufficient to sustain critical loads.
Translate generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count using an availability probability bound.
Constrain pre-islanding dispatch to maintain readiness and use advance outage warning to prepare resources.
evidence_signal: Case studies targeting 14-day islanding and 0.999 islanding-entry availability found that resource-dependent constraints preserved readiness at a modest modeled cost increase, while economic-only dispatch and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy could fail.
watch_item: Readiness guarantees depend on the assumed uncertainty bounds and generator failure-and-recovery model; the abstract reports case studies rather than field validation.
paper_title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
